claim: Synchrotron-based X-ray micro-tomography can yield 3-dimensional whole-organism images suitable for quantitative histological phenotyping of zebrafish at ~1 micron voxel resolutions.
source: To determine how synchrotron-based X-ray micro-tomography (micro-CT) can yield 3-dimensional whole-organism images suitable for quantitative histological phenotyping, we scanned whole zebrafish, a small vertebrate model with diverse tissues, at ~1 micron voxel resolutions.
evidence: The abstract describes the experimental approach and resolution achieved in the study.

claim: Micro-CT optimized for cellular characterization (histotomography) allows brain nuclei to be computationally segmented and assigned to brain regions.
source: Micro-CT optimized for cellular characterization (histotomography) allows brain nuclei to be computationally segmented and assigned to brain regions, and cell shapes and volumes to be computed for motor neurons and red blood cells.
evidence: The abstract states that brain nuclei can be computationally segmented and assigned to brain regions using histotomography.

claim: Cell shapes and volumes can be computed for motor neurons and red blood cells using histotomography.
source: Micro-CT optimized for cellular characterization (histotomography) allows brain nuclei to be computationally segmented and assigned to brain regions, and cell shapes and volumes to be computed for motor neurons and red blood cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that cell shapes and volumes can be computed for specific cell types.

claim: Individual phenotypic variation is apparent from color maps of computed densities of brain nuclei.
source: Striking individual phenotypic variation was apparent from color maps of computed densities of brain nuclei.
evidence: The abstract describes the observation of phenotypic variation through computed density maps.

claim: Histotomography allows the study of 3-dimensional structures of millimeter scale that cross multiple tissue planes.
source: Unlike histology, the histotomography also allows the study of 3-dimensional structures of millimeter scale that cross multiple tissue planes.
evidence: The abstract contrasts histotomography with traditional histology, highlighting its capability for 3D analysis.

claim: Histology has been used for over a century to visualize cellular composition and tissue architecture in millimeter- to centimeter-scale tissues from diverse multicellular organisms.
source: Histology has been used for over a century to visualize cellular composition and tissue architecture in millimeter- to centimeter-scale tissues from diverse multicellular organisms (Virchow, 1860).
evidence: The introduction provides historical context for histology with a citation.

claim: The diagnostic power of histology is dependent on the detection and description of changes in cell and tissue architecture.
source: Its diagnostic power is dependent on the detection and description of changes in cell and tissue architecture.
evidence: The introduction describes the basis of histology's diagnostic utility.

claim: Normal and abnormal cytological features indicative of physical, inflammatory, and neoplastic causes of disease are readily distinguished using established staining procedures.
source: Normal and abnormal cytological features indicative of physical, inflammatory, and neoplastic causes of disease are readily distinguished using established staining procedures (Kumar et al., 2015).
evidence: The introduction describes the capabilities of histology with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Physical sectioning introduces tissue loss and distortions that compromise complete reconstruction of tissues from serial histology sections.
source: Physical sectioning introduces tissue loss and distortions that compromise complete reconstruction of tissues from serial histology sections (Arganda-Carreras et al., 2010).
evidence: The introduction identifies a limitation of traditional histology with supporting citation.

claim: The technical demands and physical properties of paraffin blocks limit slice thickness to ~5 µm.
source: The technical demands and physical properties of paraffin blocks limit slice thickness to ~5 µm, leading to incomplete sampling and imperfect visualization of elongated structures such as vessels and large cells that extend beyond the section thickness.
evidence: The introduction describes a technical limitation of histology.

claim: Only a small fraction of any given tissue sample is studied in histology.
source: As a result, only a small fraction of any given tissue sample is studied in histology.
evidence: The introduction describes a consequence of histology's limitations.

claim: It is intractable to generate complete sets of sections for large numbers of whole organisms and impractical to align them for volumetric analysis.
source: Moreover, it is intractable to generate complete sets of sections for large numbers of whole organisms (as needed for a genetic or chemical screen) and impractical to align them for volumetric analysis.
evidence: The introduction describes practical limitations of histology for large-scale studies.

claim: Micro-CT is commonly used to study hard, mineralized tissues like bones and fossils.
source: Micro-CT is commonly used to study hard, mineralized tissues like bones and fossils (Donoghue et al., 2006; Ketcham and Carlson, 2001).
evidence: The introduction describes established applications of micro-CT with citations.

claim: Soft-tissue imaging typically requires contrast-enhancing, heavy-metal stains such as osmium tetroxide, iodine, phosphotungstic acid (PTA), or gallocyanin-chromalum.
source: Soft-tissue imaging typically requires contrast-enhancing, heavy-metal stains such as osmium tetroxide, iodine, phosphotungstic acid (PTA), or gallocyanin-chromalum (Betz et al., 2007; Metscher, 2009a; Metscher, 2009b).
evidence: The introduction describes requirements for soft-tissue micro-CT imaging with citations.

claim: Phase-based synchrotron imaging of unstained samples allows the study of development in live whole Xenopus embryos over time.
source: Phase-based synchrotron imaging of unstained samples allows the study of development in live whole Xenopus embryos over time (Moosmann et al., 2013) and of dense human cerebellar tissue (Töpperwien et al., 2018).
evidence: The introduction describes capabilities of phase-based synchrotron imaging with citations.

claim: Commercial micro-CT devices utilize polychromatic, low-flux X-ray tube sources that limit resolution and throughput.
source: Commercial micro-CT devices have been used to interrogate soft-tissue structure in diverse stained specimens (Badea et al., 2008; Batiste et al., 2004; Cheng et al., 2016a; Metscher, 2009a; Staedler et al., 2013), but these devices utilize polychromatic, low-flux X-ray tube sources that limit resolution and throughput.
evidence: The introduction describes limitations of commercial micro-CT devices with citations.

claim: Synchrotron X-ray sources have monochromatic, high-flux beams that allow rapid imaging of mm-scale samples.
source: Synchrotron X-ray sources have monochromatic, high-flux beams (Winick, 1994) that allow rapid imaging of mm-scale samples such as insects (Betz et al., 2007; Mizutani et al., 2013; van de Kamp et al., 2018), vertebrate embryos (Khonsari et al., 2014; Raj et al., 2014), zebrafish (Seo et al., 2015), and mouse somatosensory cortex (Dyer et al., 2017).
evidence: The introduction describes advantages of synchrotron sources with multiple citations.

claim: Micro-CT of larger samples such as whole mice or whole mouse organs have lacked adequate tissue contrast and/or resolution (~10 µm3) for histological phenotyping.
source: Micro-CT of larger samples such as whole mice or whole mouse organs have lacked adequate tissue contrast and/or resolution (~10 µm3) for histological phenotyping (Busse et al., 2018; Hsu et al., 2016).
evidence: The introduction describes limitations of micro-CT for larger samples with citations.

claim: Nano-CT enables imaging at higher resolution (~100 nm3) but does not provide sufficient field-of-view for mm-scale samples.
source: Conversely, nano-CT enables imaging at higher resolution (~100 nm3) but does not provide sufficient field-of-view for mm-scale samples.
evidence: The introduction describes the trade-off between resolution and field-of-view in nano-CT.

claim: Zebrafish is the largest established vertebrate model to fit in the field-of-view used in this study (juveniles are <3 mm in diameter).
source: We chose zebrafish, the largest established vertebrate model to fit in our field-of-view (juveniles are <3 mm in diameter), to determine conditions for attaining a degree of tissue contrast required for histopathological analysis across a range of tissues.
evidence: The introduction explains the rationale for choosing zebrafish as the model organism.

claim: X-ray histotomography is pan-cellular, like histology, allowing for the creation of histology-like virtual sections.
source: X-ray histotomography as developed here is pan-cellular, like histology, allowing for the creation of histology-like virtual sections, but unlike histology, can be used to study millimeter-scale phenotypes involving convoluted and branched structures such as gills, gut, vessels, and nerve tracts.
evidence: The introduction describes a key feature of histotomography.

claim: Histotomographic images provide a mechanism for quantitative histopathological analysis that facilitates the objective and reproducible study of volume, shape, and texture of cells across organisms and tissue types.
source: Histotomographic images provide a mechanism for quantitative histopathological analysis that facilitates the objective and reproducible study of volume, shape, and texture of cells across organisms and tissue types.
evidence: The introduction describes the analytical capabilities of histotomography.

claim: A beam energy of 13.8 keV was used for larval samples and 16.2 keV for juveniles due to their greater thickness.
source: A beam energy of 13.8 keV was used for the smaller, larval samples and 16.2 keV for juveniles due to their greater thickness (see Materials and methods).
evidence: The Results section describes the imaging parameters used.

claim: A 30 mm sample-to-scintillator distance provided sufficient edge enhancement to achieve histology-like contrast.
source: A 30 mm sample-to-scintillator distance provided sufficient edge enhancement to achieve histology-like contrast.
evidence: The Results section describes the optimization of imaging parameters.

claim: Monochromatic acquisitions took ~20 min, ~36 fold faster than acquisition by commercial tabletop sources.
source: Monochromatic acquisitions took ~20 min,~36 fold faster than acquisition by commercial tabletop sources (e.g.,~720 min for Xradia 500 series machines) (Metscher, 2009b).
evidence: The Results section compares acquisition times with a citation.

claim: Each pink-beam acquisition took ~20 s, ~60 fold faster than monochromatic acquisition and ~2,000 fold faster than commercial sources.
source: Each pink-beam acquisition took ~20 s,~60 fold faster than monochromatic acquisition and ~2,000 fold faster than commercial sources.
evidence: The Results section compares pink-beam acquisition times to other methods.

claim: Monochromatic acquisitions have better image quality than pink-beam, as defined by signal-to-noise ratio and pixel intensity profile.
source: Monochromatic acquisitions have better image quality than pink-beam, as defined by signal-to-noise ratio and pixel intensity profile (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The Results section compares image quality between acquisition methods with reference to a figure.

claim: No image degradation over years of repetitive synchrotron imaging was detected.
source: Notably, no image degradation over years of repetitive synchrotron imaging was detected (Lin et al., 2018).
evidence: The Results section describes sample stability with a citation.

claim: The z-axis resolution of histotomography, presented at 0.74 or 1.43 microns, is superior to the ~5 micron slice thickness of histology's conventional paraffin sections.
source: Notably, the z-axis resolution of histotomography, presented here at 0.74 or 1.43 microns, is superior to the ~5 micron slice thickness of histology's conventional paraffin sections.
evidence: The Results section compares the z-axis resolution of histotomography to traditional histology.

claim: The average spacing of striations in skeletal muscle fibers encircling the larval swim bladder is 2.16 μm (SD = 0.55 μm) based on 293 measurements.
source: The average of 293 measures = 2.16 μm (SD = 0.55 μm) is comparable with published values (Burghardt et al., 2016; Dou et al., 2008).
evidence: The Results section provides quantitative measurements with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and citations.

claim: Reconstructions of larval huli hutu at 0.743 µm3 voxel resolution allowed detection of all of hht's known histological changes.
source: Reconstructions of larval hht at 0.743 µm3 voxel resolution allowed us to detect all of hht's known histological changes, including nuclear fragmentation (karyorrhexis) that is associated with cell death, nuclear atypia (increased size, deviation from typical ovoid shape, and irregular nuclear membrane contour) in the gut, and tissue degeneration.
evidence: The Results section describes the detection of histopathological features in a mutant.

claim: The average number of nuclei in the brain region out of 5 larvae studied was 75,413 (SD = 8,547).
source: The average number of nuclei in the brain region out of 5 larvae studied was 75,413 (SD = 8,547) (Table 2).
evidence: The Results section provides quantitative data on brain nuclei counts with reference to a table.

claim: Heat-maps of cell densities revealed obvious differences between five wild-type siblings.
source: Notably, heat-maps of cell densities revealed obvious differences between five wild-type siblings.
evidence: The Results section describes phenotypic variation observed in the data.

claim: Fish 1 and 2 exhibit a shift towards lower cell density as compared with fish 3, 4, and 5, which correlates with the larger brain volumes of fish 1 and 2.
source: Comparatively, fish 1 and 2 exhibit a shift towards lower cell density as compared with fish 3, 4, and 5, which correlates with the larger brain volumes of fish 1 and 2 (Tables 2–3).
evidence: The Results section describes correlations observed in the data with reference to tables.

claim: Differences in cell density may be explained by differences in exact developmental stage.
source: These differences in cell density may be explained by differences in exact developmental stage.
evidence: The Results section provides a potential explanation for observed variation.

claim: Screening 10,000 zebrafish mutants in replicate would require ~20 years with a monochromatic synchrotron source and, if fully optimized, <1 year using pink-beam X-rays.
source: By our estimates, screening 10,000 zebrafish mutants in replicate would require ~20 years with a monochromatic synchrotron source and, if fully optimized, <1 year using pink-beam X-rays.
evidence: The Discussion section provides estimates for throughput potential.

claim: Some 70% of human protein-coding genes have at least one zebrafish orthologue.
source: The fact that some 70% of human protein-coding genes have at least one zebrafish orthologue makes this throughput potential relevant to disease modeling and the probing of human gene function (Howe et al., 2013).
evidence: The Discussion section provides context for the relevance of zebrafish studies with a citation.

claim: Fluorescence-based imaging depends on sample transparency and for optically more opaque samples requires dissection and/or physical slicing to maintain resolution.
source: Fluorescence-based imaging, however, depends on sample transparency, and for optically more opaque samples, dissection and/or physical slicing to maintain resolution without diffraction or loss of signal (Chung et al., 2013; Hama et al., 2011; Susaki et al., 2014; Watson et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion section describes limitations of fluorescence-based imaging with citations.

claim: Image quality is compromised in the presence of significant melanin pigmentation, even in transparent samples with diameters of more than about a millimeter.
source: Image quality is compromised in the presence of significant melanin pigmentation, even in transparent samples with diameters of more than about a millimeter.
evidence: The Discussion section describes a limitation of optical imaging methods.

claim: Serial block-face scanning electron microscopy has been used to image and reconstruct a mouse neocortex and the larval zebrafish brain at nanometer-scale.
source: Serial block-face scanning electron microscopy has been used to image and reconstruct a mouse neocortex (Kasthuri et al., 2015) and the larval zebrafish brain at nanometer-scale (56.4 × 56.4 × 60 nm3 resolution from 16,000 sections) (Hildebrand et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion section describes alternative imaging methods with citations.

claim: A multi-beam scanning electron microscope imaging a single cubic mm of tissue at 20 nm3 resolution can require ~3 months of continuous imaging.
source: For example, a multi-beam scanning electron microscope, imaging a single cubic mm of tissue at 20 nm3 resolution can require ~3 months of continuous imaging (Dyer et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion section describes the time requirements of alternative methods with a citation.

claim: The distribution of cell nuclei in the samples corresponded well with those seen in 54 nm thick transmission electron microscopy sections.
source: The distribution of cell nuclei in our samples corresponded well with those seen in 54 nm thick transmission electron microscopy sections (Hildebrand et al., 2017) (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The Results section validates the findings by comparison to published data with a citation and figure reference.

claim: The F1 score showed ~90% correspondence between manual and automated detections of cell nuclei.
source: The F1 score, optimized for probability threshold to balance precision and recall, showed ~90% correspondence between manual and automated detections (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section provides quantitative validation of the automated detection method with reference to a figure.

claim: The mean elongation was 1.9, 1.3, and 1.1 for RBCs, motor neurons, and brain nuclei, respectively.
source: The mean elongation was 1.9, 1.3, and 1.1 for RBCs, motor neurons, and brain nuclei, respectively.
evidence: Figure 8 caption provides quantitative measurements of cell shape.

claim: The mean volume was 99, 102, and 13 µm3 for RBCs, motor neurons, and brain nuclei, respectively.
source: The mean volume was 99, 102, and 13 µm3 for RBCs, motor neurons, and brain nuclei, respectively.
evidence: Figure 8 caption provides quantitative measurements of cell volume.

claim: Brain cell nuclei were assigned to major brain regions including the olfactory epithelia, telencephalon, diencephalon, hypothalamus, mesencephalon, metencephalon, myelencephalon, white matter, and spinal cord by cross-atlas registration.
source: We have assigned brain nuclei to major brain regions including the olfactory epithelia, telencephalon, diencephalon, hypothalamus, mesencephalon, metencephalon, myelencephalon, white matter, and spinal cord by cross-atlas registration (Raj et al., 2018; Ronneberger et al., 2012; Wullimann and Mueller, 2005).
evidence: The Results section describes the method for brain region assignment with citations.

claim: Synchrotron micro-CT studies were performed on the sector two bending magnet, hutch B (2-BM-B) of the Advanced Photon Source at Argonne National Laboratory.
source: Micro-CT studies were performed on the sector two bending magnet, hutch B (2-BM-B) of the Advanced Photon Source at Argonne National Laboratory for both single-energy and multi-energy acquisitions (Figure 1).
evidence: The Results section describes the experimental setup.

claim: Beam energies for monochromatic imaging were optimized for contrast-to-noise ratio across a range of sample diameters and concentrations of tungsten.
source: Beam energies for monochromatic imaging were optimized for contrast-to-noise ratio across a range of sample diameters and concentrations of tungsten (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section describes the optimization process with reference to a figure.

claim: Sample-to-scintillator distance was adjusted to optimize the magnitude of phase contrast-based edge enhancement.
source: Sample-to-scintillator distance was adjusted to optimize the magnitude of phase contrast-based edge enhancement (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The Results section describes the optimization of imaging parameters with reference to a figure.

claim: The volumetric field of view was 1.5 mm3 for 0.743 µm3 voxels using a 10X objective lens, and 3 mm3 with 1.43 µm3 voxels using a 5X objective.
source: The volumetric field of view was 1.5 mm3 for 0.743 µm3 voxels using a 10X objective lens, and 3 mm3 with 1.43 µm3 voxels using a 5X objective.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides technical specifications.

claim: 1501 projections were obtained over 180 degrees (1 projection every 0.12 degrees) for monochromatic imaging.
source: 1501 projections were obtained over 180 degrees (1 projection every 0.12 degrees) with a 2048-by-2048 pixel CoolSnap HQ CCD camera (Photometrics, AZ, USA).
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides technical details of the acquisition.

claim: A polychromatic 'pink-beam' covering 10–30 keV was used to obtain 1600 projections over 192 degrees.
source: A polychromatic 'pink-beam' covering 10–30 keV, was used to obtain 1600 projections over 192 degrees (1 per 0.12 degrees) with a 2048-by-2048 pixel CoolSnap HQ CCD camera.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides technical details of pink-beam acquisition.

claim: Wild-type zebrafish (Ekkwill strain) and the huli hutu mutant were reared at an average temperature of 28°C in a recirculating system with a 14:10 hr light:dark cycle.
source: Wild-type zebrafish (Ekkwill strain) and the huli hutu mutant (Mohideen et al., 2003) were reared at an average temperature of 28°C in a recirculating system with a 14:10 hr light:dark cycle (Copper et al., 2018).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the animal husbandry conditions with citations.

claim: Specimens were stained with 0.3% phosphotungstic acid (PTA) for 24 hr at room temperature with gentle agitation.
source: Specimens were stained with 0.3% phosphotungstic acid (PTA) (diluted from a 1% w/v stock solution at a ratio of 3:7 in 100% EtOH) for 24 hr at room temperature with gentle agitation.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the staining protocol.

claim: PTA is used widely in histology and electron microscopy for staining collagen and other connective tissue.
source: This metallic stain is used widely in histology and electron microscopy for staining collagen and other connective tissue (Bloom and Aghajanian, 1968; Bulmer, 1962).
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides context for the staining method with citations.

claim: Total sample preparation time takes 5 days.
source: Total sample preparation time takes 5 days.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides information about the preparation timeline.

claim: ViewTool is an open-access and web-based multiplanar viewer available at http://3D.fish.
source: To allow users to inspect the data without having to download the full resolution volumes, we developed ViewTool, an open-access and web-based multiplanar viewer (http://3D.fish) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the data sharing platform.

claim: ViewTool is partly based on the open-access project OpenSeaDragon.
source: ViewTool is partly based on the open-access project OpenSeaDragon (https://openseadragon.github.io/), and combines radiology and digital pathology workflows into a seamless experience to provide user-friendly access to our 3D data.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the technical basis of ViewTool.

claim: Semi-automated segmentation was performed using Elastix version 4.8, an open-source registration software.
source: Semi-automated segmentation was performed using Elastix version 4.8, an open-source registration software (Klein 2010, http://elastix.isi.uu.nl/).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the software used for segmentation.

claim: Cell nuclei were distinguished from background using a supervised learning approach with Ilastik version 1.3.
source: Using a supervised learning approach, we distinguished brain cell nuclei from background by training examples using Ilastik version 1.3 (Sommer et al., 2011), a simple, user-friendly, open-source tool for interactive image classification, segmentation and analysis (http://ilastik.org/).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the cell detection method with a citation.

claim: A probability threshold and size filter (80% or higher probability containing at least 8 voxels, ~3.5 µm3) were used to detect individual cell nuclei.
source: From these measures, a probability threshold and size filter (80% or higher probability containing at least 8 voxels,~3.5 µm3) were used to detect individual cell nuclei.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the parameters used for cell detection.

claim: The detected brain regions were derived from segmented volumes of the larval (4 dpf) reference fish from the ViBE-Z zebrafish brain atlas.
source: The detected brain regions were derived from segmented volumes of the larval (4 dpf) reference fish from the ViBE-Z zebrafish brain atlas (Ronneberger et al., 2012), which was used for the primary registration onto one of our 5 dpf samples.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the atlas used for brain region assignment with a citation.

claim: Validation of region detection was performed by cross-referencing to a histology-based developmental brain atlas.
source: Validation of region detection was performed by cross-referencing to a histology-based developmental brain atlas (Wullimann and Mueller, 2005) and manual segmentation was used to correct areas of inaccurate registration.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the validation approach with a citation.

claim: Synchrotron X-ray flux is orders of magnitude more brilliant than commercial tube sources.
source: Synchrotron X-ray flux is orders of magnitude more brilliant than commercial tube sources, allowing imaging times short enough for high sample-number imaging projects (Winick, 1994).
evidence: The Results section describes the advantage of synchrotron sources with a citation.

claim: Plastic embedding of specimens adds sample stability for image re-acquisition with improved micro-CT implementations.
source: Plastic embedding of specimens, while not essential for synchrotron micro-CT, adds sample stability (Lin et al., 2018) f image re-acquisition with improved micro-CT implementations.
evidence: The Discussion section describes a benefit of plastic embedding with a citation.

claim: Increasing field-of-view beyond ~2.7 mm will be needed to image the full width of mature zebrafish.
source: Increasing field-of-view beyond ~2.7 mm (used for histotomography of juveniles at 1.4 micron isotropic voxel resolution) will be needed to image of the full width of mature zebrafish, and will be facilitated by larger imaging chip arrays.
evidence: The Discussion section identifies a technical limitation and potential solution.

claim: Condensed chromosomes are about one micron in diameter, requiring true 0.5 micron pixel/voxel resolution for detection.
source: Condensed chromosomes are about one micron in diameter, requiring true 0.5 micron pixel/voxel resolution for detection.
evidence: The Discussion section describes a resolution requirement for detecting specific cellular features.

claim: X-ray histotomography approaches the ideal of comprehensive and quantitative phenotyping for tissue samples and model organisms that lie in the mm-to-cm length scale.
source: The work shown here approaches the ideal of comprehensive and quantitative phenotyping for tissue samples and model organisms that lie in the mm-to-cm length scale, such as the zebrafish.
evidence: The Discussion section summarizes the capabilities of the method.

claim: X-ray histotomography allows for full volume imaging of replicate samples at cellular resolution, distinguishing neighboring cells and resolving nuclear morphologies in optically opaque larval and juvenile zebrafish specimens.
source: Indeed, X-ray histotomography allows for full volume imaging of replicate samples at cellular resolution, distinguishing neighboring cells and resolving nuclear morphologies in optically opaque larval and juvenile zebrafish specimens.
evidence: The Discussion section summarizes the key capabilities demonstrated.

claim: Extending this work to Drosophila, C. elegans, and Arabidopsis, and to tissue samples from larger organisms such as mouse and human would enable cross-species phenotypic analyses.
source: Extending this work to Drosophila, C. elegans, and Arabidopsis, and to tissue samples from larger organisms such as mouse and human would enable cross-species phenotypic analyses, leading to a more universal understanding of tissue architecture and morphological phenotype.
evidence: The Discussion section discusses potential future applications.

claim: Histotomographic data are ideal for real-time visualization using virtual reality technologies such as syGlass.
source: Histotomographic data are also ideal for real-time visualization using virtual reality technologies such as syGlass (Pidhorskyi et al., 2018).
evidence: The Discussion section describes a potential application with a citation.

claim: Repositories of high-resolution images from a full complement of human and other organismal tissues would facilitate cross-correlations between model system and human phenotypes.
source: Repositories of high-resolution images from a full complement of human and other organismal tissues would facilitate cross-correlations between model system and human phenotypes (Regev et al., 2017; Rozenblatt-Rosen et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion section discusses the potential value of data repositories with citations.

claim: The huli hutu mutant shows a range of subtle to obvious histological changes across all cell types and tissues.
source: To probe the potential ability of X-ray histotomography to detect subtle histopathological change in a whole organism, we used a mutant, huli hutu (hht), that is known to show a range of subtle to obvious histological changes across all cell types and tissues (Mohideen et al., 2003) (Figure 6, Video 6).
evidence: The Results section describes the characteristics of the mutant used with a citation.

claim: Nuclear fragments are commonly two microns or less in diameter.
source: Nuclear fragments are commonly two microns or less in diameter.
evidence: The Results section provides information about the size of cellular features.

claim: The pneumatic duct cannot be reliably assessed by histology on account of its small size and tortuous shape.
source: This structure cannot be reliably assessed by histology on account of its small size and tortuous shape.
evidence: The Results section describes a limitation of traditional histology for assessing specific structures.

claim: The isotropic nature of histotomography enables reslicing in any plane of section without distortion.
source: The isotropic nature of histotomography enables reslicing in any plane of section without distortion.
evidence: The Results section describes a key advantage of histotomography.

claim: Dynamic reslicing allows the study of either longitudinal, perpendicular, or other planar virtual sections of the gut at cellular resolution.
source: Dynamic reslicing (cutting the same volume digitally in multiple planes) allows the study of either longitudinal, perpendicular, or other planar virtual sections of the gut at cellular resolution (Figure 4).
evidence: The Results section describes the capability for multi-planar analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: The ability to generate full sets of cross-sections of convoluted structures for histological phenotyping within a single modality is unprecedented.
source: As far as we are aware, the ability to generate full sets of cross-sections of convoluted structures (such as the gut of juvenile zebrafish) for histological phenotyping within a single modality is unprecedented.
evidence: The Results section claims novelty of the approach.

claim: Virtual sectioning and 3D rendering can be used to study any tissue in the fish.
source: Virtual sectioning and 3D rendering can be used to study any tissue in the fish, as illustrated for the neuronal cells in the eye, cartilaginous elements of the notochord, the squamous patch of the dorsum of the pharynx, nucleated red blood cells in the heart, and the pneumatic duct and goblet cells of the intestine of whole juvenile (33 dpf) and larval (five dpf) specimens in Figure 5 and Figure 6, respectively.
evidence: The Results section describes the broad applicability of the method with references to figures.

claim: Digital zebrafish allow tissues and cell nuclei to be visualized across organ systems, including the integumentary, hematopoietic, respiratory, genitourinary, musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, nervous and sensory systems.
source: In sum, our digital zebrafish allow tissues and cell nuclei to be visualized across organ systems, including the integumentary, hematopoietic, respiratory, genitourinary, musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, nervous and sensory systems (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Video 5).
evidence: The Results section summarizes the comprehensive nature of the imaging with references to figures and videos.

claim: Brain cell nuclei can be distinguished from other stained objects based on shape (elongation) and volume.
source: For example, brain cell nuclei can be distinguished from other stained objects based on shape (elongation) and volume.
evidence: The Results section describes the basis for computational cell type discrimination.

claim: Computational measurements of shape and volume of manually segmented red blood cells (RBCs) and motor neurons (n = 20 each) were different, in agreement with morphological differences that are readily apparent in histology.
source: As anticipated, computational measurements of shape and volume of manually segmented red blood cells (RBCs) and motor neurons (n = 20 each) were different, in agreement with morphological differences that are readily apparent in histology (Figure 8A).
evidence: The Results section describes quantitative validation of cell type differences with reference to a figure.

claim: RBCs and motor neurons are more elongated than typical brain nuclei, which are more spherical.
source: In addition, RBCs and motor neurons are more elongated than typical brain nuclei, which are more spherical.
evidence: The Results section describes morphological differences between cell types.

claim: RBCs are typically flat and oval, while motor neurons are more 'tear drop' shaped.
source: Specifically, RBCs are typically flat and oval, while motor neurons are more 'tear drop' shaped.
evidence: The Results section describes specific morphological characteristics of cell types.

claim: Motor neurons are larger than typical brain nuclei in volume.
source: Other cell differences include the volume, with motor neurons being larger than typical brain nuclei.
evidence: The Results section describes volumetric differences between cell types.

claim: The PTA staining patterns of the cytoplasm of RBCs and motor neurons are different in appearance from those of other cells.
source: The PTA staining patterns of the cytoplasm of RBCs and motor neurons are different in appearance from those of other cells.
evidence: The Results section describes differences in staining patterns between cell types.

claim: The current resolution is sufficient to readily distinguish cell types.
source: From the measurements shown, it is apparent that our current resolution is sufficient to readily distinguish cell types.
evidence: The Results section concludes that the resolution is adequate for cell type discrimination.

claim: Three 75 µm3 regions of neural cell nuclei were manually annotated and compared against classifier results for location and counts.
source: Three 75 µm3 regions of neural cell nuclei were manually annotated and compared against classifier results for location and counts.
evidence: The Results section describes the validation approach for automated cell detection.

claim: Features used in the classification include intensity, edges, and texture.
source: Features that were used in the classification including intensity (pixel value with various smoothing), edges (gradient, Laplacian of Gaussian, and difference of Gaussians) and texture (structured tensor of eigenvalues, Hessian of Gaussian eigenvalues).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the features used for machine learning classification.

claim: The random forest classifier assigned a probability of being a nucleus to any given pixel.
source: The random forest classifier assigned a probability of being a nucleus to any given pixel.
evidence: The Results section describes the output of the classification algorithm.

claim: Brain cell nuclei have high probabilities, while blood vessels and background have low probabilities in the nuclear labeling.
source: The results of nuclear labeling based on the nuclear training set demonstrate that, as expected, brain cell nuclei have high probabilities, while blood vessels and background have low probabilities.
evidence: The Results section describes the performance of the classification.

claim: Automatically detected cell nuclei were checked against those manually detected and categorized as true-positive, false negative, or false positive.
source: Automatically detected cell nuclei were checked against those manually detected and categorized as true-positive (manual and automatic detected), false negative (manually detected but automatically undetected), or false positive (manually undetected but automatically detected).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the validation methodology.

claim: Imaging and analysis of multiple specimens at multiple ages is necessary to establish knowledge of normal statistical variation in gross and microscopic anatomy.
source: Imaging and analysis of multiple specimens at multiple ages is necessary to establish a knowledge of normal statistical variation in gross and microscopic anatomy across organ systems that is needed for automated detection of 'abnormal' phenotypes.
evidence: The Discussion section describes requirements for comprehensive phenotyping.

claim: Whole specimen histotomography datasets are well-suited for automated organ and cellular level detection that can be used as a scaffold for morphological lifespan atlases.
source: Whole specimen histotomography datasets are well-suited for automated organ and cellular level detection that can be used as a scaffold for morphological lifespan atlases, capturing the extent of normal phenotypic variation at cellular, tissue, and organismal scales.
evidence: The Discussion section describes potential applications of the method.

claim: The pan-cellular nature of histotomography makes it ideal for cross-referencing with images from focused modalities involving transgenic or whole-mount stained organisms.
source: The pan-cellular nature of histotomography makes it ideal for cross-referencing with images from focused (e.g. fluorescence-based) modalities involving transgenic or whole-mount stained organisms; this would involve fixation, staining and histotomographic imaging of the fluorescently studied specimens.
evidence: The Discussion section describes potential integration with other imaging modalities.

claim: The addition of tissue-, cell-, and/or protein-specific micro-CT stains would enable targeted analyses and cross-atlas comparisons of explicit constituents.
source: Conversely, the addition of tissue-, cell-, and/or protein-specific micro-CT stains would enable targeted analyses and cross-atlas comparisons of explicit constituents within the full context of a scanned sample or organism (Metscher and Müller, 2011).
evidence: The Discussion section discusses potential enhancements to the method with a citation.

claim: Further optimization will be needed to resolve mitotic chromosomes.
source: Further optimization will be needed to resolve a key characteristic of proliferating cells: mitotic chromosomes.
evidence: The Discussion section identifies a current limitation.

claim: The molecular specificity of fluorescence-based phenotyping is poorly suited for large-scale screens that require phenotyping across all cell types.
source: The molecular specificity of fluorescence-based phenotyping is poorly suited for large-scale screens that require phenotyping across all cell types.
evidence: The Discussion section describes a limitation of fluorescence-based approaches for comprehensive phenotyping.

claim: Three-dimensional tissue imaging methods based on ultrathin serial tissue sections or block-face imaging have ultrastructural cellular resolution, but become intractable for large scale studies of specimens larger than ~1 cubic millimeter in minimum dimension.
source: Three-dimensional tissue imaging methods based on ultrathin serial tissue sections or block-face imaging have ultrastructural cellular resolution, but becomes intractable for large scale studies of specimens larger than ~1 cubic millimeter in minimum dimension.
evidence: The Discussion section describes limitations of alternative high-resolution methods.

claim: 3D reconstructions based on serial sectioning are time-consuming enough to be infeasible for interrogating all tissues in the numbers of specimens required for toxicology or genetic screens.
source: 3D reconstructions based on serial sectioning are time-consuming enough to be infeasible for interrogating all tissues in the numbers of specimens required for toxicology or genetic screens.
evidence: The Discussion section describes throughput limitations of serial sectioning methods.

claim: Ideal comprehensive anatomical phenotyping would include quantitative characterization of tissue architecture and cellular features in addition to measures of larger features such as organ size, vascular structure, nerve structure, and body shape.
source: Ideal comprehensive anatomical phenotyping would include quantitative characterization of tissue architecture and cellular features in addition to measures of larger features such as organ size, vascular structure, nerve structure, and body shape.
evidence: The Discussion section describes the goals of comprehensive phenotyping.

claim: Computational phenotyping will require the development of detailed 3D atlases.
source: Comprehensive computational phenotyping will thus require the development of detailed 3D atlases.
evidence: The Discussion section identifies a requirement for future work.

claim: High-throughput primary screens by pink-beam could be followed by higher-contrast monochromatic imaging of samples that show evidence of phenotypic change.
source: High-throughput primary screens by pink-beam could be followed by higher-contrast monochromatic imaging of samples that show evidence of phenotypic change.
evidence: The Discussion section proposes a workflow for large-scale screening.

claim: The unprecedented depth of zebrafish tissue phenotyping enabled by histotomography has the potential to enrich conclusions from mouse phenome projects.
source: The unprecedented depth of zebrafish tissue phenotyping enabled by histotomography has the potential to enrich conclusions from mouse phenome projects (Dickinson et al., 2016; Hsu et al., 2016).
evidence: The Discussion section discusses potential impact on other research areas with citations.

claim: Optical imaging modalities such as light sheet fluorescence microscopy are ideal for in vivo studies and resolve 3D sub-micron features.
source: Optical imaging modalities such as light sheet fluorescence microscopy are ideal for in vivo studies (McDole et al., 2018), and resolve 3D sub-micron features.
evidence: The Discussion section describes capabilities of alternative imaging methods with a citation.

claim: Serial block-face scanning electron microscopy studies made it possible to define precise neurological and circulatory relationships across the entire brain.
source: These studies made it possible to define precise neurological and circulatory relationships across the entire brain.
evidence: The Discussion section describes the capabilities of serial block-face scanning electron microscopy.

claim: Genetic phenomics may involve the study of mutants for each zebrafish protein-encoding gene (>26,000) and non-coding functional element.
source: Genetic phenomics may involve, for example, the study of mutants for each zebrafish protein-encoding gene (>26,000) and non-coding functional element.
evidence: The Discussion section describes the scope of potential genetic screens.

claim: Assuming specific conditions, screening 10,000 zebrafish mutants in replicate would require ~40 years with monochromatic source or ~1 year using pink-beam.
source: Assuming: (i) a 5 min set up time per specimen, (ii) 10 replicates per condition, (iii) three scans per fish, (iv) a synchrotron availability of 100 scanning days per year and 10 hr of scanning time per scanning day, and (v) ability to multiplex five larval specimens at a time without increasing acquisition time, screening 20,000 larval mutants would require ~40 years with monochromatic source or ~1 year using pink-beam.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides detailed throughput estimates based on specific assumptions.

claim: There is potential for higher throughput via robotic sample swapping for monochromatic and polychromatic sources and/or increased multiplexing with pink-beam.
source: There is potential for higher throughput via robotic sample swapping for monochromatic and polychromatic sources and/or increased multiplexing with pink-beam.
evidence: The Materials and methods section discusses potential improvements to throughput.

claim: Estimates of throughput would be affected by the proportion of specimens that are juvenile or adult, since those are likely to be imaged individually.
source: Estimates of throughput would also be affected by the proportion of specimens that are juvenile or adult, since those are likely to be imaged individually, and require either multiple segmental scans per fish or spiral CT as used for humans.
evidence: The Materials and methods section discusses factors affecting throughput estimates.

claim: In X-ray based imaging modalities, the choice of imaging energy determines both the contrast between different tissue types and the noise level in the image.
source: In X-ray based imaging modalities, including micro-CT, the choice of imaging energy determines both the contrast between different tissue types and the noise level in the image.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes fundamental principles of X-ray imaging.

claim: The contrast is based on the difference in energy-dependent absorption coefficient between the materials of interest, and the noise is determined by the transmitted flux of X-rays.
source: The contrast is based on the difference in energy-dependent absorption coefficient between the materials of interest, and the noise is determined by the transmitted flux of X-rays.
evidence: The Materials and methods section explains the physical basis of contrast and noise in X-ray imaging.

claim: A contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) is generally maximized at some intermediate energy that depends on the concentration and amounts of various tissues present.
source: A contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) is generally maximized at some intermediate energy that depends on the concentration and amounts of various tissues present.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the optimization principle for imaging energy.

claim: Metal-stained tissue tomography is associated with the potential addition of X-ray absorption edges introducing additional structure into the energy-dependence of attenuation coefficients.
source: Metal-stained tissue tomography is associated with the potential addition of X-ray absorption edges introducing additional structure into the energy-dependence of attenuation coefficients.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes a consideration for metal-stained samples.

claim: A simple model from Spanne (1989) was used to investigate tradeoffs in energy selection.
source: To investigate these tradeoffs, we made use of a simple but powerful model from Spanne (1989) that assumes the presence of a small circular contrasting detail at the center of a circular absorbing background.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the modeling approach used with a citation.

claim: The model shows a clear optimal energy range just above the tungsten L1 edge at 12 keV with strong fall off below the L3 edge at 10.2 and again above about 16 keV.
source: These are shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and both sets of plots show a clear optimal energy range just above the tungsten L1 edge at 12 keV with strong fall off below the L3 edge at 10.2 and again above about 16 keV.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the results of energy optimization modeling with reference to a figure.

claim: All PTA stained larval data were acquired at the pre-calibrated 13.8 keV monochromator setting based on the energy optimization.
source: We thus chose to acquire all PTA stained larval data at the pre-calibrated 13.8 keV monochromator setting.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the imaging parameter choice based on optimization.

claim: For larger juvenile fish of diameter >3 mm, the CNR peak is broader, justifying the use of higher, more penetrating X-ray energies.
source: For larger juvenile fish of diameter >3 mm, the CNR peak is broader, justifying the use of higher, more penetrating X-ray energies.
evidence: The Materials and methods section explains the rationale for different energy settings for different sample sizes.

claim: The 16.2 keV monochromator setting was chosen for juvenile specimens.
source: Therefore, we chose the 16.2 keV monochromator setting for juvenile specimens.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the imaging parameter choice for juvenile samples.

claim: The coherence of synchrotron radiation allows for imaging that is sensitive to phase shifts in the incident X-ray wave front.
source: The coherence of synchrotron radiation allows for imaging that is sensitive to phase shifts in the incident X-ray wave front caused by variations in the real part of the complex index of refraction.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the physical basis of phase-contrast imaging.

claim: Interference fringes develop in the transmitted intensity pattern as it propagates beyond the sample.
source: The latter techniques rely on the fact that interference fringes develop in the transmitted intensity pattern as it propagates beyond the sample.
evidence: The Materials and methods section explains the mechanism of phase-contrast enhancement.

claim: Larval reconstructions at SSDs of 20, 30, 40 and 50 mm were generated to optimize phase contrast.
source: Herein, we generated larval (five dpf) reconstructions at SSDs of 20, 30, 40 and 50 mm.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the experimental approach to optimize phase contrast.

claim: The SSD of 20 mm caused edges of nuclei to appear blurry.
source: The SSD of 20 mm caused edges of nuclei to appear blurry.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the results of phase contrast optimization.

claim: SSDs of 30 or 40 mm yielded a degree of edge perception resembling that achieved in glass slide histology.
source: SSDs of 30 or 40 mm yielded a degree of edge perception resembling that achieved in glass slide histology.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the optimal range for phase contrast.

claim: SSDs of 50 mm and larger caused edge effects to begin to look 'artificial' compared with traditional histology and transmission electron microscopy.
source: Subjectively SSDs of 50 mm and larger (data not shown) caused edge effects to begin to look 'artificial' compared with traditional histology and transmission electron microscopy.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the upper limit for optimal phase contrast.

claim: Exaggerated phase effects can diminish perceived resolution.
source: Exaggerated phase effects can diminish perceived resolution.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes a potential problem with excessive phase contrast.

claim: An 'ideal' SSD depends upon the specific structures being defined.
source: Notably, an 'ideal' SSD depends upon the specific structures being defined.
evidence: The Materials and methods section notes that optimization is structure-dependent.

claim: Line profiles through the periodic retinal cells show that higher SSDs give rise to line profiles with a higher modulation depth.
source: Line profiles through the periodic retinal cells show that higher SSDs give rise to line profiles with a higher modulation depth, with the greatest benefit achieved around 30 and 40 mm SSD and strong evidence of overshooting and bias above 50 mm SSD.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes quantitative analysis of phase contrast effects.

claim: An SDD of 30 mm was used for all subsequent acquisitions based on phase contrast optimization.
source: Based on these considerations, we used an SDD of 30 mm for all subsequent acquisitions.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the final parameter choice.

claim: CT reconstruction was done using TomoPy, an open-source package from Argonne National Labs.
source: CT reconstruction was done using TomoPy, an open-source package from Argonne National Labs (http://tomopy.readthedocs.io).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the reconstruction software used.

claim: Some of the image processing was conducted in Fiji/ImageJ2.
source: Some of the image processing was conducted in Fiji/ImageJ2 (https://fiji.sc/).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes image processing software used.

claim: Software used for volumetric visualizations include Avizo version 9.4 and VGStudio Max 2.1.
source: Software used for volumetric visualizations in this manuscript include Avizo version 9.4 (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) and VGStudio Max 2.1 (Volume Graphics, Heidelberg, Germany).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes visualization software used.

claim: The file sizes associated with synchrotron micro-CT are on the order of ~100 GB per larval or juvenile zebrafish.
source: The file sizes associated with synchrotron micro-CT are on the order of ~100 GB per larval or juvenile zebrafish, making scans difficult to view for people with standard computational resources.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the data size challenge.

claim: Orthogonal image z-stacks are downsampled using JPG compression before being served to end users through Amazon Web Services' Simple Storage Service (AWS 3).
source: Orthogonal image z-stacks are downsampled using JPG compression before being served to end users through Amazon Web Services' Simple Storage Service (AWS 3).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the data delivery approach for ViewTool.

claim: Only every fourth slice is currently shown in the viewer by default for bandwidth considerations.
source: For bandwidth considerations, only every fourth slice is currently shown in the viewer by default.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes a technical limitation of the web viewer.

claim: ViewTool's code was written in client-side JavaScript, HTML and CSS, requires no download, and has no server requirement to run the basic implementation.
source: ViewTool's code was written in client-side JavaScript, HTML and CSS, requires no download, and has no server requirement to run the basic implementation.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the technical implementation of ViewTool.

claim: All registrations were performed in two parts: an affine registration for optimizing initialization positions followed by a landmark based thin-plate spline registration.
source: All registrations were performed in two parts: an affine registration for optimizing initialization positions of both images followed by a landmark based thin-plate spline registration.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the registration approach.

claim: Landmarks were manually marked on corresponding anatomical regions for registration.
source: Landmarks were manually marked on corresponding anatomical regions.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the manual component of the registration process.

claim: Manual segmentations were performed using the open-source software, ITK-SNAP version 3.4.
source: Manual segmentations were performed using the open-source software, ITK-SNAP version 3.4 (Yushkevich et al., 2006) (http://www.itksnap.org).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the segmentation software used with a citation.

claim: The ViBE-Z database and atlas are publicly available.
source: The ViBE-Z database and atlas are publicly available (http://vibez.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/) (Ronneberger et al., 2012).
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides information about atlas availability with a citation.

claim: ViewTool is publically available at http://3D.fish.
source: ViewTool is publically available (http://3D.fish).
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides information about data availability.

claim: Digital histology is publicly available from the Zebrafish Lifespan Atlas.
source: Digital histology is publicly available from our Zebrafish Lifespan Atlas (http://bio-atlas.psu.edu) (Cheng, 2004).
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides information about data availability with a citation.

claim: Registered and unregistered 8-bit reconstructions of the heads of five zebrafish larvae involved in analysis are available on the Dryad Digital Repository.
source: Registered and unregistered 8-bit reconstructions of the heads of five zebrafish larvae involved in analysis are available on the Dryad Digital Repository (https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.4nb12g2), along with scripts written for cell nuclei detection, analysis, and sample registration.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides information about data and code availability.

claim: Full resolution scans, including raw projection data, are available from researchers upon request.
source: Full resolution scans, including raw projection data, are available from researchers upon request as a download or by transfer to physical media.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides information about data availability.

claim: All procedures on live animals were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at the Pennsylvania State University.
source: All procedures on live animals were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at the Pennsylvania State University.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides ethical approval information.

claim: Fish were fed three times a day a diet consisting of brine shrimp and flake food.
source: Fish were fed three times a day a diet consisting of brine shrimp and flake food.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes animal husbandry procedures.

claim: All fish were staged according to the zebrafish developmental staging series of Kimmel et al. (1995).
source: All fish were staged according to the zebrafish developmental staging series of Kimmel et al. (1995).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the staging method with a citation.

claim: Juvenile fish were starved for at least 24 hr before fixation to improve fixation and reduce the volume of gut contents.
source: To improve fixation and reduce the volume of gut contents, we starved juvenile fish for at least 24 hr for a 10 mm specimen.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes a sample preparation procedure.

claim: Fixed zebrafish specimens were rinsed 3 times in 1X PBS for 10 min followed by being submerged in 35% ethyl alcohol (EtOH) for 20 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
source: Fixed zebrafish specimens were rinsed 3 times in 1X PBS for 10 min followed by being submerged in 35% ethyl alcohol (EtOH) for 20 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes sample preparation steps.

claim: After staining, each specimen was infiltrated by sequential submerging in increasing concentrations of EtOH (70%, 90%, 95%, and 100%) for 30 min intervals at room temperature with gentle agitation.
source: After staining, each specimen was infiltrated by sequential submerging in increasing concentrations of EtOH (70%, 90%, 95%, and 100%) for 30 min intervals at room temperature with gentle agitation.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes sample preparation steps.

claim: The samples were embedded in glycol methacrylate or EMBed-812 in Kapton tubing.
source: The samples were then embedded in glycol methacrylate (Polysciences, Inc, Warrington, PA) or EMBed-812 (Electron Microscopy Sciences, Hatfield, PA) in Kapton tubing (Small Parts, Inc, Logansport, IN).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the embedding procedure.

claim: The tubing provides structural support with high thermal stability.
source: The tubing provides structural support with high thermal stability.
evidence: The Materials and methods section explains the purpose of the tubing.

claim: Generation of the ENU-mutagenized mutant hht was previously described.
source: Generation of the ENU-mutagenized mutant hht was previously described (Mohideen et al., 2003).
evidence: The Materials and methods section references prior work with a citation.

claim: The hht line was maintained as heterozygotes due to the recessive larval-lethal nature of the mutation.
source: The hht line was maintained as heterozygotes due to the recessive larval-lethal nature of the mutation.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the genetic maintenance of the mutant line.

claim: Homozygous mutant larvae were identified by a combination of gross phenotypes, including small eyes, small head, dorsally curved body, and enlarged yolk.
source: Homozygous mutant larvae were identified by a combination of gross phenotypes, including small eyes, small head, dorsally curved body, and enlarged yolk, that are easily detected under a low-power stereomicroscope at ≥3 dpf.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the phenotypic identification of mutants.

claim: Quasi-parallel X-rays from beamline 2-BM-B are used to acquire projection images of intact, fixed, and PTA-stained whole zebrafish.
source: Quasi-parallel X-rays from beamline 2-BM-B are used to acquire projection images of an intact, fixed, and PTA-stained whole zebrafish.
evidence: Figure 1 caption describes the imaging setup.

claim: Total imaging time is ~20 min per monochromatic acquisition and ~20 s per pink-beam acquisition.
source: Total imaging time is ~20 min per monochromatic acquisition (sample-to-scintillator distance = 30 mm) and ~20 s per pink-beam acquisition (sample-to-scintillator distance = 25 mm).

claim: Each fish requires 3 to 5 acquisitions for whole-organism imaging.
source: Each fish requires 3 to 5 acquisitions.
evidence: Figure 1 caption provides information about the number of acquisitions needed.

claim: Removal of the polyimide tubing is necessary for natural color light photography, but not for successful X-ray image acquisition.
source: Removal of the polyimide tubing is necessary for natural color light photography, but not for successful X-ray image acquisition.
